1 (regression). extension_install._recorded_path_target now handles the two kinds of path record differently:
- A plain record (from a typed install, an older aelix version, or source add) still gets the file:// URI when the URI can carry it. When installer_arg raises CatalogError, it returns the user's own string: the absolute path with its extras, which is the round-6 (1fcd4704) hand-off. This covers extras on a project with no [project] name. It also covers a '#' in a typed path, because the fallback applies to any CatalogError from installer_arg.
- A catalog record (the URI written since round 7) keeps the URI hand-off, always.

_cmd_update now wraps each record in try/except Exception. It prints 'Error: could not update <label>: <reason>' through safe_for_terminal, counts that record as 2 (not run), and continues with the rest. The summary says '1 failed' and the run exits non-zero. The docstrings and the _upgrade_source comment are updated.

- The guide's 'What this protects against' section and its bundled copy, which are still identical.

Installer configuration that uv discovers itself (ADR-0200, _uv_config_files) is stated as a known limit. The follow-up issue text is in follow_ups and in .omc/probes/131-live/fix7b/follow-up-issue.txt. It is not filed.

- A %-escape gets 'pip cuts the path at a '%23' and clones another repository', with the advice to write git+file:///<absolute path> without escapes.
The file: messages are unchanged. A real-backend row measures the claims: git ignores the host on both backends, and %23 is cut by pip but not by uv.

owner_decisions: File the follow-up issue whose text is in follow_ups and in .omc/probes/131-live/fix7b/follow-up-issue.txt: uv config in the cwd can redirect a catalog package install. It is stated in all four docs as a known limit of #131 and has not been filed.
When update catches an error from one record, it counts that record as exit 2 (not run). The alternative is 1 (installer failed). It still outranks 3, and the summary lists the record as failed.

The typed-record fallback applies to any CatalogError from installer_arg, not only a missing project name. So a typed path that contains '#' also keeps its round-6 plain-string hand-off on update, instead of crashing.
follow_ups: Issue text - Title: uv configuration in the current directory can redirect a catalog package install. Body: With the uv backend, discover install of a trusted catalog entry whose source is a package name runs uv pip install <name> from the user's cwd. uv reads uv.toml and pyproject.toml [tool.uv] from the cwd and every parent (and the user-level uv.toml). aelix honours that on purpose (ADR-0200, _uv_config_files, _uv_has_own_index_config). In a cloned repository, [tool.uv] find-links = ['./w'] (or uv.toml find-links / index settings) makes the catalog's package name resolve to a wheel the repo ships. Measured on 7dc0e05d (.omc/probes/131-live/verify7/uvconfig-head.txt): source local-ext with --index-url file://<org dir> installed local-ext==9.9 from ./w (CWD-DECOY) on uv, exit 0; pip read neither file. ADR-0255 section 12 limits #131 to never resolving a source against the cwd and never handing the installer a string it would read from there, and lists this as a known limit. Options: (a) run the uv child for catalog installs from a neutral directory; (b) --no-config plus the user file via UV_CONFIG_FILE; (c) warn or refuse when a project uv config with index or find-links keys is above the cwd; (d) document only. Mind _uv_has_own_index_config and typed installs. Acceptance: that measurement as a row, plus ADR-0200 and ADR-0255 section 12 updated.

nonblocking.title: The update fallback also catches the '#' refusal, not only a missing project name
nonblocking.detail: _recorded_path_target falls back to the plain string on ANY CatalogError from installer_arg, so it also catches the '#' refusal, not just the missing-project-name case the brief named. A plain record holding '#' (a typed install, an older aelix's record, or source add) is now handed raw on update. uv cuts it at '#' and installs the sibling. On 7dc0e05d the same update stopped with a traceback and installed nothing. For a typed record this repeats what the typed install itself did, and the paths are absolute, so #131's cwd guarantee holds. ADR-0255 §12/§14 and the CHANGELOG say a plain record the URI cannot carry is updated as it was installed. Two things are still slightly off: the guide line 'a record an older aelix wrote (the plain path) is turned into the URI when update reads it' is too broad for a '#' record, and the VERIFY ROUND 7 section does not mention '#'. The patch summary does disclose it. Consider narrowing the fallback to the nameless-extras error and letting '#' fail as an isolated, reported error.
